chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the Muhrim (person in Ihram) catches game by mistake, he is upon him the expiation. If he catches it a second time by mistake, he is upon him the expiation always if it is by mistake. If he catches it intentionally, he is upon him the expiation. If he catches it a second time intentionally, then he is among whom Allah takes vengeance from him and there is not upon him the expiation."

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever upon him is due the ransom of the game and he is Muhrim for Hajj, he slaughters what is due upon him or slaughters it in Mina. And if he is Muhrim for Umrah, he slaughters or slaughters in Mecca.

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a person in Ihram who accidentally or intentionally catches game?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between accidental and intentional hunting violations during Ihram, noting that repeated intentional acts incur divine vengeance rather than a fixed expiation. It further specifies the geographical requirements for the expiatory sacrifice, mandating Mina for Hajj pilgrims and Mecca for Umrah pilgrims, reflecting the specific sanctity of these locations in Shia fiqh.
